summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -4 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy 0; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Cheese +12.9%; weakest: Lean hogs -22.8%. Key releases ahead: US Average Hourly Earnings m/m (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Non-Farm Employment Change (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Unemployment Rate (11-06 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.86% (-42 bp in a month), 2-year 4.51% (-26 bp); 2s10s curve +35 bp (-16 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.00% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 102.30 (+0.1% in a month, +4.1% YTD). USD/BRL 5.503 (+10.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.665 (-0.6%); USD/MXN 18.60 (+3.5%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -5.4% in a month (+7.8% YTD); VIX 25.6. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 90.37 $/bbl (+3.2% in a month), Brent 97.77, ULSD 4.341 $/gal (-3.0%), natural gas 3.00 (-14.5%). Crude little changed on the month. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -5.9% in a month, Shanghai Composite -5.0%, Hang Seng +1.5%, yuan +0.6% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 6 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (18%); S&P GSCI -4.1% in a month; gold -1.5%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
